Source. The witness command's `TPMA_NV` field becomes `0x84012001`, which includes `TPMA_NV_ORDERLY`; later logic therefore treats the index data as RAM-backed orderly state.
The same public descriptor's trailing bytes `01 f4` become `target->dataSize = 500`, the exact boundary value later used to size the orderly-RAM entry.

On the zeroed startup buffer, `NvRamGetEnd()` is the base of `s_indexOrderlyRam`, so `remaining` is 512. With the witness's `size = 500`, `needed` is `12 + 500 = 512`, and the helper returns true for the exact-full fit.
Because `ORDERLY` is set and step 3's helper returned true, this rejection branch is not taken. The request therefore survives the RAM-space check instead of failing with `TPM_RC_NV_SPACE`.
Inside the orderly-only RAM path, libtpms computes one entry size as `sizeof(NV_RAM_HEADER) + 500 = 512`, so a single entry will consume the entire `RAM_INDEX_SPACE`.
Starting at the empty buffer base, libtpms writes the 12-byte header and zero-fills 500 data bytes, so this one orderly entry occupies bytes `0..511` of `s_indexOrderlyRam`.
After the exact-full entry from step 6, `end` advances to `RAM_ORDERLY_END`. The terminator guard is therefore false at the boundary, so no 0-sized `NV_RAM_HEADER` is written after the entry.
libtpms records that orderly RAM changed by setting `g_updateNV |= UT_ORDERLY`, which is the cleanup-time trigger for staging `s_indexOrderlyRam` to NV before `NvCommit()`.

At command cleanup, `ExecCommand`'s `if (g_updateNV == UT_ORDERLY)` branch invokes this write, so the malformed exact-full orderly-RAM image is staged into backing NV storage right before `NvCommit()` marshals the permanent state.

The same malformed 512-byte image is reloaded from NV into local stack array `indexOrderlyRam[512]`. AddressSanitizer identifies this exact stack object as the overread buffer in frame `PERSISTENT_ALL_Marshal`.

On the first marshal iteration, `offset` is 0 and this header read yields `nrh.size = 512`. The same iteration's `if (offset + nrh.size > array_size)` check does not break because `0 + 512 > 512` is false, so the exact-fit entry is treated as valid and marshalled.
Root cause. After the first and only valid entry, `offset` becomes exactly 512. Vulnerable code immediately loops again without checking whether another `NV_RAM_HEADER` still fits at that boundary.

After marshalling an exact-fit entry, this increment makes `offset == array_size == 512`, but vulnerable code immediately iterates again instead of checking whether `offset + sizeof(NV_RAM_HEADER) > array_size` and stopping. The fix adds that missing post-increment guard at this point.
AddressSanitizer sink. On the next loop iteration after `offset` reaches 512, `nrhp` is `indexOrderlyRam + 512`, so this 4-byte header read goes one word past the end of the 512-byte stack buffer.
